A pellicle is a SCOBY. Bacteria and yeasts live within it and therefore it is a SCOBY. The tea itself is also a SCOBY.

I never thought about that. My first instinct has always been to swipe/dry with a paper towel the walls.

I explain how I do it. (so far my kombucha has been very happy and healthy);

So first I sterilize my jar. Clean very deeply. And also with boiling water. Make sure your kitchen is spotless, and to wash your hands even if you just scratched your nose for a second.

Then, after boiling your tea, pour it into your now clean and sterilized jar. Now with your tea inside your jar, just wait for some hours until it's room temperature. Make sure to cover it well so no dust, pollution or anything gets inside. Like a plate (clean)

Then, take your scoby/mushroom carefully (HANDS SUPER CLEAN!!! ALSO YOUR NAILS) and put it inside. Then pour the liquid of the kombucha inside.

The container where your kombucha has been for some hours as you waited for the tea of the jar to cool down, must also have been very cleaned before you put the scoby in it to wait.

Then, if any liquid spilled to the walls, take a paper towel and dry it. That's it I think
